cover.headline: A well-run jeweller, fairly priced: the gold price has already done the heavy lifting
cover.lead: Kalyan Jewellers is India's second-largest listed jeweller: 546 stores across India, the Middle East, the US/UK and its online brand Candere. Execution has been excellent: revenue has quadrupled in five years and profit grew 89% in FY26 as franchise partners funded new stores and debt was repaid. But most of the recent growth is the gold price, not more grams sold, and margins are thin (6-7% EBITDA) and drifting down as franchise stores share profit. We value Kalyan the way the street does, on **P/E: 30x Sep-28E EPS of ₹19.3** (brokers use 35-40x). That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**, just short of our 15% BUY threshold: **we initiate with HOLD.** EV/EBITDA (₹562) confirms it; the DCF (₹421) warns that cash flows alone support less. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The growth is real, but mostly gold-price inflation
arguments.p: Revenue grew 43% in FY26 and 38% in Q1FY27 (ex-bullion), but Indian jewellery volumes fell 24% in 2025 (World Gold Council). Kalyan grows grams faster than the market through new stores, yet a large part of the growth is a 30-40% rise in the gold price. If gold flattens, growth falls to the store-addition rate: ~15-18%.

arguments.h: The franchise model is clever, but it caps margins
arguments.p: Two-thirds of India stores are now franchise-owned, company-operated (FOCO): partners put up the capital, Kalyan runs the store and shares the margin. This freed capital to repay ₹1,000 cr of debt, but EBITDA margin falls as the mix shifts (India 5.9% in Q1FY27, 5.1% excluding a one-off gain). Management now guides on PBT margin, not EBITDA.

arguments.h: Valuation: reasonable on the street's own yardstick, but no bargain
arguments.p: Jewellers are priced on P/E. Kalyan's one-year-forward P/E has averaged ~40x since 2023; the whole sector has since de-rated ~24% (Titan 65x vs 86x norm). Applying that to Kalyan gives 30x, or {{dcf.tp|inr}} on Sep-28E earnings. The street pays 35-40x on more optimistic earnings. Our DCF (₹421) says cash flows alone support less.

In May 2026 the government raised gold import duty from 6% to 15% and the Prime Minister asked citizens to defer gold purchases. ICRA expects industry volumes to fall ~15% in FY27. Q2FY27 growth already slowed to 26% (from 38% in Q1).

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (by 14-Nov-2026): margin after the gold-exchange push and the duty-gain one-offs.
Gold price direction and any rollback of the 15% import duty.
Store openings: 84 Kalyan (all franchise) + 50 Candere planned in FY27.
Promoter pledge (~25% of promoter shares) and any further block deals.

sections.title: A gold jeweller with three businesses and an unusual franchise model

blocks.p: Kalyan sells gold, diamond and precious-stone jewellery through large showrooms. About 70% of what it sells is plain gold jewellery (studded pieces are ~30% in India and ~16% in the Middle East), so the price a customer pays is mostly the value of the gold plus a making charge. That is why revenue moves with the gold price and why margins are thin: Kalyan earns roughly 12% gross and 6-7% EBITDA on each rupee of sales.

blocks.p: Since 2022 almost all new Kalyan showrooms are **franchise-owned, company-operated (FOCO)**. A partner, usually a financial investor rather than a jeweller, pays for the store and the entire inventory, and bears the running costs except staff. Kalyan designs, stocks, staffs and runs the store under its brand, and the two share the margin. Partners earn about 14% on their capital. For Kalyan this means: (1) no capital needed for new stores, so debt has been repaid; (2) a lower EBITDA margin because profit is shared; (3) a higher return on capital. FOCO share of India revenue rose from 40% (Q3FY25) to 57% (Q1FY27).

blocks.callout: **An accounting point worth knowing:** Kalyan books the jewellery it ships to franchise stores as its own revenue (₹15,050 cr in FY26, about half of standalone sales), with up to 180 days' credit. This is allowed, but it means part of reported revenue is sales into its own franchise network rather than to end-customers.

sections.title: A huge, slow-growing market where organised players take share

blocks.p: India's gems and jewellery retail market was worth about ₹12.9 lakh cr in FY26 (CRISIL), roughly 80-85% gold. In value it has grown ~21% a year since FY22, but almost entirely because of the gold price: jewellery demand in tonnes fell from ~563t in 2024 to ~431t in 2025. CRISIL expects only 4-5% value growth to FY30 as high prices hurt affordability. The real opportunity for chains like Kalyan is **share shift**: organised jewellers hold 37-42% today and are expected to reach 45-50% by FY30, helped by mandatory hallmarking and consumer trust.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Kalyan's advantages are **scale, trust and a capital-light expansion engine**; these are real and explain why it grows faster than the market. But jewellery is a trust business with a commodity inside it: customers can compare gold rates and making charges across the street. Kalyan has **no pricing power**: its EBITDA margin has stayed at 6-8% for a decade, half of Titan's jewellery margin. A business like this deserves a growth multiple, but not a premium-brand multiple.

sections.title: Revenue has quadrupled in five years; margins have not moved

blocks.p: Kalyan's revenue rose from ₹8,573 cr in FY21 (a COVID year) to ₹35,743 cr in FY26, about 33% a year, and was up 46% in Q1FY27. Net profit rose faster, from a small loss to ₹1,350 cr, because interest and other fixed costs grew much more slowly than sales. But the EBITDA margin has stayed in a narrow 6-8% band for a decade. Jewellery retail is a high-volume, thin-margin trade: most of the selling price is the gold itself.

pair.title: Revenue: ~33% a year since FY21
Net profit: up 6x since FY22
EBITDA margin: stuck at 6-8%
Interest has barely grown while revenue tripled

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the profit story is operating leverage, not pricing power. Interest was ₹390 cr in FY18 and ₹499 cr in FY26 while revenue grew 3.4x, so interest fell from 3.7% to 1.4% of sales. The franchise (FOCO) model lets Kalyan open stores with partners' capital, which is why debt has not grown with the business.

sections.title: Earnings quality: one-offs, gold hedges and franchise sales

bullets: **Customs duty swings.** Duty changes revalue the stock already paid for: a ₹124 cr loss in FY25 (duty cut) and gains of ~₹41 cr in Q1FY27 and ~₹60 cr expected in Q2FY27 (duty hike). Strip these out when comparing margins.

**Gold hedging.** Almost all gold inventory is hedged through gold metal loans, gold on lease and futures, so gold-price moves largely offset in profit. This is prudent, but hedge accounting makes quarterly gross margins noisy.
**Sales to franchisees.** About half of standalone revenue is jewellery shipped to franchise stores on up to 180 days' credit. Receivables rose faster than sales in FY26.
**Bullion sales.** From Q1FY27 Kalyan sells some bullion (₹581 cr in Q1); reported revenue growth (+46%) overstates jewellery growth (+38%).
**Exceptional items.** FY26 included a ₹41.5 cr charge for the new Labour Codes.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** No qualification from the auditor (Walker Chandiok since 2024), and hedging is conservative. But one-offs, franchise sales and bullion make headline growth and margins harder to read than at a simple retailer.

sections.title: Inventory is the business: ₹14,175 cr of gold on the shelves

blocks.p: A jeweller's main asset is its stock. Kalyan held ₹14,175 cr of inventory at March 2026, about 70% of total assets. It funds this with three sources: (1) gold metal loans and working-capital debt from banks (short-term borrowings ₹4,111 cr), (2) advances from customers, mostly monthly gold-savings schemes (₹4,396 cr), and (3) suppliers and franchise partners. Inventory days have fallen from 272 in FY21 to ~165, mainly because franchise stores carry less company-funded stock.

pair.title: Inventory days have fallen by 100+ days
Operating cash flow positive every year since FY21

blocks.callout: **What to watch:** borrowings rose to ₹6,117 cr in FY26 (₹4,111 cr bank and gold loans plus ₹2,006 cr lease liabilities) because the gold price jump made every gram of stock more expensive. Gold metal loans are partly a natural hedge: the loan is denominated in gold, so a rise in the gold price raises the liability and the inventory together. Note also that reported operating cash flow counts new gold loans as an operating inflow (₹1,251 cr in FY26); excluding them, FY26 operating cash flow was close to zero. Growth is funded by gold borrowing.

sections.title: Ownership: a promoter-controlled company, with foreign investors stepping back

blocks.p: The promoter family (T.S. Kalyanaraman and sons) holds 62.85%. Warburg Pincus, the private-equity backer since 2014, exited completely in 2023-24, mostly to Indian mutual funds; the promoter bought the last 2.36% at ₹535. Motilal Oswal Midcap Fund is the largest outside holder (9.17%).

blocks.p: The bull case on the street rests on 20%+ earnings growth for several years, capital-light franchise growth and a 30% discount to Titan (brokers apply 35-40x forward earnings). We agree on the quality of execution. We disagree on two points: (1) how much of the growth is the gold price, which can reverse; and (2) whether a 6% EBITDA-margin business deserves a multiple close to Titan's, which earns about twice the margin.

Brokers value jewellers the way they value consumer retailers: on **P/E on earnings two years out**. Four of the five brokers whose method we could find use P/E on 2028 earnings, at 35-40x; only ICICI Securities uses a DCF. We therefore set our target the same way, so that our number is comparable with theirs. The difference between us and the street is in the inputs (our EPS is ~8% below consensus, and our multiple is lower), not in the method.

sections.title: Our honest summary: great business, close to fair value

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's best-executing mass-market jeweller, growing ~20% a year with a capital-light franchise engine, a strong board and falling debt.

**What you are paying:** 29.2x FY28E earnings, below Kalyan's own history and at its widest discount to Titan. On the street's method (P/E) and our inputs, the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). That is just short of our 15% BUY threshold, and the DCF warns that cash flows support a lower price if growth slows.

statementNotes.sales@FY21: COVID lockdowns closed stores for much of Q1FY21.
statementNotes.sales@FY23: Strong wedding season and store additions; gold price up.
statementNotes.sales@FY24: FOCO-led store expansion outside South India, plus higher gold prices.
statementNotes.sales@FY26: Gold price surge (~+40-50% YoY) plus ~170 new stores, mostly franchise.
statementNotes.pat@FY22: Recovery from the COVID-hit FY21 loss.
statementNotes.pat@FY26: Revenue +43% with interest up only 18%; margin held.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY25: Customs duty on gold cut from 15% to 6% (Jul-2024): inventory losses on high-duty stock and pass-through of lower prices.
statementNotes.sales@FY27E: GAM: +20%; H2 slows against the gold-price surge of Q3-Q4FY26 and the duty hike.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY27E: Franchise mix and gold-exchange promotions keep margin near 6.4%.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Kalyan Jewellers (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven revenue (India, Middle East, Candere); valued on a 15-year DCF.

segments.name: India (Kalyan showrooms)
segments._why: Q1FY27 +38% and Q2FY27 +27% (ex-bullion) on the gold price; H2 faces a very high base (Q4FY26 +68%), the May-2026 duty hike and the PM's appeal to defer gold buying, so we assume ~12% in H2. FY28-29: ~85 franchise stores a year (~20% store growth) plus mid-single-digit same-store growth.
segments._marginWhy: 6.8% in FY26; 5.9% in Q1FY27 including a ₹41 cr one-off duty gain (5.1% underlying). Franchise (FOCO) stores share margin with partners, and gold-exchange sales dilute margin by 20-30bp. We assume ~6%, below FY26.

segments.name: Middle East
segments._why: Q1FY27 +29%, Q2FY27 +12%. Store count flat at 38; growth is mostly the gold price and same-store sales.

segments.name: Candere (online + stores)
segments._why: Q2FY27 +64%; ~50 new stores in FY27 (138 at Sep-26).
segments._marginWhy: Turned marginally profitable in H2FY26; EBITDA not disclosed. We assume a slow climb.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Reconciling items: other operating income less eliminations (negative = adds to EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: FY26 reported EBITDA (₹2,562 cr, Screener) exceeds the sum of segment EBITDA (₹2,412 cr) by ~₹150 cr: other operating income (royalty from franchisees), less inter-segment eliminations.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex below ₹250 cr a year (ICRA) because franchise partners fund new stores; plus lease principal (~₹280 cr in FY26), since rent sits below EBITDA under Ind AS 116.
assumptions._depWhy: Q1FY27 depreciation ₹115 cr (~₹470 cr a year) ≈ 9.7% of gross block.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt, so no treasury income; other income is entered separately.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: FY26 normal other income ₹208 cr (interest on deposits, misc.); FY27 includes part of the ₹102 cr non-core land sale.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹499 cr; Q1FY27 ₹108 cr. Non-gold-loan debt in India fully repaid by Sep-2026; gold metal loans (~₹3,600 cr) remain and cost more as the gold price rises.

dcf._betaWhy: Discretionary spend tied to gold prices; market-like sensitivity.
dcf._tgWhy: Jewellery demand tracks nominal GDP and the gold price; 6% allows for slowing volumes as gold gets dearer.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Asset-light franchise model keeps capex low.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Gold stays high and demand holds; franchise roll-out of 90+ stores a year continues; India margin back to ~6.8% as cash-for-gold and studded mix help.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Higher duty and a falling gold price hit value growth; franchise dilution pushes India margin to ~5.3%; growth slows to low teens.

operatingDebt.label: Gold metal loans (inventory funding)
operatingDebt._why: Gold borrowed from banks to stock showrooms, repaid in gold; ~10% of revenue at Mar-26. Treated as working-capital funding (as the company, ICRA and brokers do), not as financing debt.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Kalyan (Jefferies, Citi, MOFSL, BOBCAPS all use P/E on 2028 EPS). 30x = Kalyan's 40x median one-year-forward P/E since 2023, cut by the 24% sector de-rating (Titan at 65x vs its 86x five-year median). Bull 36x (half the de-rating), bear 24x (Kalyan's 2023 levels).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 6%. Thin margins and inventory keep free cash low, so the DCF sits below the market multiples.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Adjusts for debt. 17x Sep-28E EBITDA is consistent with 30x P/E after interest and tax; Kalyan trades at 20.5x trailing today (30x median since 2023).
